name: Amazon Ads
summary: Spend, impressions, clicks and sales per Sponsored Products campaign from your Amazon Ads profiles.
description: Signs in with Amazon (Login with Amazon) and reads every advertising profile the sign-in can reach, in North America, Europe and the Far East, read-only: Sponsored Products campaigns and their daily numbers from Amazon's reports.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

features.note: Login with Amazon.
Amazon reviews each application before granting access.
Amazon's conversion events API is in beta.
Hashed lists go to Amazon DSP and Amazon Marketing Cloud audiences, not Sponsored Products.

limits.text: The Amazon Ads API needs an application and Amazon's approval before any call works.
Outflare reads Sponsored Products campaigns only, not Sponsored Brands or Sponsored Display.
Outflare syncs Amazon campaigns only, not their ad groups or ads.

name: Apple Ads
summary: Spend, impressions, taps and installs per campaign from your Apple Ads (formerly Apple Search Ads) accounts.
description: Uses your own Apple Ads API user. In Apple Ads, invite a user with an API role (API Account Read Only is enough), sign in as that user, upload a public key under Account Settings, API, and paste the client id, team id and key id Apple shows there, with the private key. Read-only: installs are measured in your app, so there is nothing to send back.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

features.note: OAuth client credentials signed with your own key pair.
An account admin gives a user an API role; Apple doesn't review the app.
Ads open the App Store; installs are measured in the app.

limits.text: An account admin invites the API user in the Apple Ads app, and that user pastes the public key there.
Daily report rows reach back at most 90 days; older numbers come only by week or month.
Outflare syncs Apple Ads campaigns only, not their ad groups or ads.

name: Google Ads
summary: Spend, clicks and conversions per campaign from your Google Ads accounts.
description: Signs in with Google and reads every Google Ads account the sign-in can see, including accounts under a manager account. Google also asks for a developer token: create one in your own Google Ads manager account (Admin, API Center) and add it after signing in. It never changes your campaigns; it sends conversions only to the conversion actions you choose under Paid ads, and adds people only to the Customer Match lists your journeys name.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

features.note: A developer token is needed; Basic and Standard access need an application to Google.
Customer Match lists.

limits.text: A developer token with Explorer access allows 2,880 operations a day on live accounts; Basic access allows 15,000.
Basic and Standard access are applied for with a form, and Standard access needs a manual review.

name: LinkedIn Ads
summary: Spend, impressions, clicks and conversions per campaign from your LinkedIn ad accounts.
description: Signs in with LinkedIn and reads every ad account the member can see, with read-only access. Conversions are LinkedIn's website conversions as LinkedIn counts them.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

features.note: LinkedIn approves each app for the Advertising API.
The Development tier edits up to five ad accounts; Standard has no cap.
Needs separate approval for the Conversions API.
Needs separate approval for the Matched Audiences API.

limits.text: The Advertising API needs an application approved by LinkedIn before an app can read ad accounts.
The Conversions API and the Matched Audiences API each need their own approval from LinkedIn.
In the Development tier the API can edit at most five ad accounts; the Standard tier is requested with a support ticket.
Outflare reads LinkedIn spend only; it doesn't send conversions or fill audiences yet.
Outflare syncs LinkedIn campaigns only, not their creatives.

name: Meta Ads
summary: Spend, clicks and conversions per campaign from your Facebook and Instagram ad accounts.
description: Reads every ad account a token can see, with read-only access. The simplest way: in your Meta Business Settings, Users, System users, create a system user, give it the ad accounts, and generate a token with the ads_read permission. Conversions are Meta's standard events (purchases, leads, registrations, trials, subscriptions). To send conversions back through the Conversions API, also assign the system user to your pixel (Business Settings, Data sources, Datasets). For journeys to add people to your customer list audiences, give the token ads_management too and accept the Custom Audience terms in your ad account.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

features.note: Standard access covers ad accounts your business owns or was granted; wider use goes through App Review.

limits.text: Customer list audiences work only after Meta's Custom Audience terms are accepted for the ad account.
Insights reach back 37 months; since January 2026, hourly breakdowns reach back 13 months and frequency 6 months.

name: Microsoft Advertising
summary: Spend, clicks and conversions per campaign from your Microsoft Advertising (Bing) accounts.
description: Signs in with Microsoft and reads every Microsoft Advertising account the sign-in can see. Microsoft also asks for a developer token: get your own from the Microsoft Advertising developer portal (Account, Request token) and add it after signing in. It never changes your campaigns; it sends offline conversions only to the goals you choose under Paid ads.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

features.note: A Super Admin requests the developer token in the developer settings.
Offline conversions.
Customer Match lists, through the Bulk API.

limits.text: The developer token is requested by a Super Admin in Microsoft Advertising's developer settings.
Only a limited number of reports can be generating at once; more wait until earlier ones finish.
Outflare doesn't fill Customer Match lists yet, though the Bulk API takes them.
Outflare syncs Microsoft Advertising campaigns only, not their ad groups or ads.

name: Outbrain Ads
summary: Spend, impressions, clicks and conversions per campaign from your Outbrain marketers.
description: Uses your own Outbrain login, once Outbrain has given it Amplify API access (apply on Outbrain's developer site). Outflare trades the username and password for an API token every few weeks and reads every marketer the login can see, read-only.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

features.note: An Outbrain username and password are traded for a token.
Amplify API access is requested from Outbrain.
The API manages conversion definitions; the pixel counts conversions.
Segments come from pixel rules or campaign clickers.

limits.text: Amplify API access is requested from Outbrain with a form before any call works.
The API has no call that takes conversions; it only manages conversion definitions for the pixel.
Segments are built from pixel rules or campaign clickers; the API has no customer list upload.
Performance reporting allows 30 requests a minute per marketer, and its numbers run 10 to 30 minutes behind.
Tokens last 30 days, and a user can ask for a new one at most twice an hour.
Outflare syncs Outbrain campaigns only, not their promoted links.

name: Pinterest Ads
summary: Spend, impressions, clicks and conversions per campaign from your Pinterest ad accounts.
description: Signs in with Pinterest and reads every ad account you can see, read-only; add a conversion access token to send conversions back through the Conversions API.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

features.note: New apps get Trial access; Standard access needs an upgrade request.

limits.text: Trial access is limited to a daily number of calls per app; Standard access needs an upgrade request with a video demo.
Outflare syncs Pinterest campaigns only, not their ad groups or ads.

name: Reddit Ads
summary: Spend, impressions and clicks per campaign from your Reddit ad accounts.
description: Signs in with Reddit and reads every ad account of every business the account belongs to, with read-only access; add a Conversions API token to send conversions back. Separate from organic Reddit, which posts and listens from your brand's own account.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

features.note: Ads API access is granted to a developer app on request.

limits.text: Outflare syncs Reddit campaigns only, not their ad groups or ads.

name: Snapchat Ads
summary: Spend, impressions and swipes per campaign from your Snapchat ad accounts.
description: Signs in with Snapchat and reads every ad account of every organization you belong to, read-only; conversions go back to your Snap Pixel through the Conversions API.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

features.note: The OAuth app is made in Ads Manager under Business Details.

limits.text: Outflare syncs Snapchat campaigns only, not their ad squads or ads.

name: Taboola Ads
summary: Spend, impressions, clicks and conversions per campaign from your Taboola advertiser accounts.
description: Uses your own Backstage API credentials: ask your Taboola account manager for API access, and paste the client id and secret they issue. A network's credentials read every advertiser account under it. Read-only; conversions go back to your event-based conversions as server-to-server actions, matched on Taboola's click id.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

features.note: OAuth client credentials issued by Taboola.
Existing customers make keys on the API Keys page or get them from their account manager.
Server-to-server events matched on the click id.
First-party audiences.

limits.text: API credentials come from Taboola, on the API Keys page or from the account manager; there is no sign-in flow.
Access tokens last 12 hours and come with no refresh token.
Accounts made after October 4, 2026 have tiered read and write rate limits; Tier 6 allows the fewest requests.
Outflare doesn't fill Taboola first-party audiences yet, though the API can add users to them.
Outflare syncs Taboola campaigns only, not their items.

name: TikTok Ads
summary: Spend, impressions, clicks and conversions per campaign from your TikTok ad accounts.
description: Signs in with TikTok For Business and reads the ad accounts you grant, read-only; conversions go back to your TikTok pixel through the Events API. To add more ad accounts later, connect again and grant them.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

features.note: TikTok reviews each developer app.
Events API.

limits.text: Outflare syncs TikTok campaigns only, not their ad groups or ads.

name: X Ads
summary: Spend, impressions and clicks per campaign from your X ad accounts.
description: Uses your own X developer app, once X has approved it for the Ads API (apply in the developer portal; approval can take a few weeks). Paste the app's API key and secret and the access token and secret of the account that runs your ads. Read-only.
pricing: Free API; ad spend stays on your own account

features.note: OAuth 1.0a.
X approves Ads API access for each developer app.

limits.text: Ads API access is requested separately for each developer app, through X's access form.
Outflare reads X spend only; it doesn't send conversions back yet.
Outflare syncs X campaigns only, not their line items or ads.

name: Amplitude
summary: Active users, page views, top pages and event counts from Amplitude.
description: Reads one project with its API key and secret key. Traffic uses active users and the [Amplitude] Page Viewed event from the browser SDK.
pricing: Free tier

limits.text: Dashboard REST queries share a budget of 108,000 cost an hour and 5 requests at once across all REST endpoints.
Raw events become available in the Export API about 2 hours after Amplitude receives them.
One export request returns at most 4 GB and covers at most 365 days.
Outflare reads dashboard queries, not raw events from the Export API.

name: Bing Webmaster Tools
summary: Clicks, impressions and the search queries people used on Bing before visiting your site.
description: Reads every verified site in your Bing Webmaster Tools account. Bing keeps about six months of search data.
pricing: Free

limits.text: Search data starts when a site is added to Bing Webmaster Tools; earlier history can't be recovered.
URL submission allows up to 10,000 URLs a day per domain, and Bing can set a lower quota for a site.
Outflare doesn't submit URLs to Bing for indexing.

name: Cloudflare Web Analytics
summary: Page views, visits, top pages and referrers from Cloudflare's free Web Analytics.
description: Reads every Web Analytics site on one Cloudflare account. Cloudflare counts visits and page views but not unique visitors.
pricing: Free

limits.text: Only 7 days are kept unsampled; older data is aggregated, and query results can be sampled.
Sites not proxied through Cloudflare are limited to 10 per account unless support raises it.
The GraphQL Analytics API allows 300 queries every 5 minutes by default.

name: Fathom Analytics
summary: Visitors, pages, referrers and event conversions from Fathom.
description: Reads every site on the account with an API key. Events count as conversions.
pricing: Paid plans

features.note: Fathom can show Google Search Console data once it is linked in the Fathom app.

limits.text: The included API tier allows 600 requests an hour and 5 at once, across all endpoints.
More API capacity needs a paid API tier, from 1,000 up to 16,000 requests an hour.
Events can't be created over the API; they appear once the site tracks them.

name: Google Analytics
summary: Visitors, top pages, traffic sources and key events from Google Analytics 4.
description: Signs in with Google (or uses a service account key) and reads any GA4 property the account can see, with read-only access. Pick the property once, or name it on each call. Conversions are GA4 key events. The same sign-in also connects Search Console.
pricing: Free

features.note: Raw events come only through the BigQuery export, not the reporting API.

limits.text: A standard property allows 200,000 report tokens a day and 10 requests at once; Analytics 360 allows more.
Reports can take 24 to 48 hours to process new data, so the latest days may still change.
The reporting API has no raw events; the BigQuery export has them, capped at 1 million events a day on standard properties.
Outflare doesn't read the realtime report, which covers the last 30 minutes.

name: Google Search Console
summary: What people search on Google before they click through to your site, and how you rank.
description: Signs in with Google (or uses a service account key) and reads every Search Console property the account can see, with read-only access. Domain properties show as sc-domain:example.com. The same sign-in also connects Google Analytics.
pricing: Free

features.note: A fixed set of dimensions (query, page, country, device, date) and metrics.
Row-level data comes only through the bulk export to BigQuery.

limits.text: Search data usually arrives two to three days late.
The API returns at most 50,000 rows a day per search type, sorted by clicks, so rare queries are left out.
URL Inspection allows 2,000 checks a day and 600 a minute per property.
Asking Google to index a page is done in the Search Console app; the Indexing API covers only job postings and livestreams.

name: Matomo
summary: Visitors, pages, referrers, events and goal conversions from Matomo, cloud or self-hosted.
description: Reads every site the token can view. The token is sent in the request body, never the address.
pricing: Free (self-hosted)

limits.text: Self-hosted reports are only as fresh as the last archiving run, which Matomo advises running hourly with cron.
Raw visit exports from the Live API can be slow or time out on large sites; Matomo suggests running them once a day.
Outflare reads aggregated reports, not raw visit details from the Live API.

name: Microsoft Clarity
summary: Sessions, visitors and frustration signals (rage and dead clicks) from Clarity, for the last three days.
description: Clarity's export API only covers the last one to three days and allows ten calls a day per project, so Outflare keeps each answer for six hours. Use it for a recent snapshot, not history.
pricing: Free

features.note: Up to three dimensions from a fixed list, over the last three days.

limits.text: The export API allows 10 requests a day per project.
It covers only the last one to three days; older data can't be read over the API.
Each request takes at most three dimensions and returns at most 1,000 rows, without paging.

name: Mixpanel
summary: Page views, pages, referrers and event counts from Mixpanel.
description: Uses a service account. Traffic comes from Mixpanel's page view event ($mp_web_page_view unless you name another). Mixpanel allows about 60 report queries an hour, so Outflare keeps each answer for an hour.
pricing: Free tier

limits.text: The Query API allows 60 queries an hour and 5 at once per project.
The raw event export allows 60 queries an hour and 3 a second per project.
JQL, Mixpanel's custom query language, is in maintenance mode, and its queries time out after 2 minutes.
Outflare reads report queries, not the raw event export.

name: Plausible
summary: Visitors, pages, sources and goal conversions from Plausible, cloud or self-hosted.
description: Reads one site with a Stats API key. Goals count as conversions.
pricing: Paid plans

limits.text: On Plausible's cloud, the Stats API needs the Business plan or higher; the Growth plan has no API access.
A Stats API key allows 600 requests an hour by default; more capacity is by request to Plausible.
Creating and managing sites over the API (the Sites API) needs an Enterprise plan.

name: PostHog
summary: Visitors, pages, referrers and custom events from PostHog. Sign in with PostHog Cloud, US or EU, or use a personal API key.
description: Signs in with PostHog and reads the projects you allow, with read-only access to queries. A personal API key works too, and is the way for self-hosted PostHog. Visitors are distinct people with a $pageview; sources are the referring domain.
pricing: Free tier

features.note: A hobby deployment on one machine, not meant for large volumes.

limits.text: The query API allows 2,400 requests an hour, 240 a minute and 3 queries running at once per project.
Queries made with a personal API key also draw on an hourly read budget and fail until it refills.
Bulk or recurring exports of events and persons aren't supported over the query API; PostHog's batch exports do that.

name: Simple Analytics
summary: Visitors, pages and referrers from Simple Analytics.
description: Reads one website. Public dashboards need only the domain; private ones need an API key and your user id.
pricing: Paid plans

limits.text: The Export API for raw page views and events needs a plan that includes it.
Adding websites over the Admin API needs a Business or Enterprise plan.
The free plan keeps 30 days of history.
Outflare reads the aggregated Stats API, not raw data points from the Export API.

name: Umami
summary: Visitors, pages, referrers and events from Umami, cloud or self-hosted.
description: Umami Cloud: paste an API key. Self-hosted: give the address and a user that can view the websites; Outflare signs in for each report.
pricing: Free (self-hosted)

limits.text: API keys on Umami Cloud need the Pro plan or higher.
Each Umami Cloud API key allows 50 calls every 15 seconds.
Some routes, such as user management, aren't available with an Umami Cloud API key.

name: Vercel Web Analytics
summary: Page views, visitors, top pages, referrers and custom events from Vercel Web Analytics.
description: Reads every project on one Vercel account or team. Only production traffic counts, as on Vercel's own dashboard. Projects need Web Analytics turned on.
pricing: Free on Hobby, more events on Pro

features.note: Only through a Vercel integration; a direct connection uses an access token.
One breakdown dimension per query, with filters.

limits.text: Aggregate queries break down by one dimension at a time and return at most 100 rows.
Queries reach back only as far as the plan's reporting window.
Counts cover production traffic only, from when Web Analytics was turned on.

name: Cal.com
summary: Count meetings leads book through your Cal.com links.
description: Reads your Cal.com bookings and their attendees. Nothing is changed in Cal.com.
pricing: Free

limits.text: API keys are limited to 120 requests a minute; more needs a request to Cal.com support and may cost extra.
A new OAuth client stays pending until Cal.com reviews and approves it.
Outflare reads accepted bookings every 15 minutes and doesn't subscribe to Cal.com webhooks yet.

name: Calendly
summary: Count meetings leads book through your Calendly links.
description: Reads scheduled events for your Calendly organization and their invitees. Nothing is changed in Calendly.
pricing: Included with paid Calendly plans

features.note: Needs a paid Calendly plan on the account that creates the subscription.
Through the Scheduling API, which needs a paid Calendly plan.

limits.text: Webhook subscriptions need a paid Calendly plan (Standard or above) on the account they are made for.
Booking meetings through the Scheduling API needs a paid Calendly plan.
API rate limits are enforced on accounts on the Free plan.
Outflare reads scheduled events every 15 minutes and doesn't use Calendly webhooks yet.

name: Google Calendar
summary: Count meetings booked with leads, from any Google Workspace or Gmail calendar.
description: Reads events from one calendar (the primary one unless calendar_id is set) and keeps only those with a lead or a lead's colleague among the guests. Nothing is written to the calendar.
pricing: Free

features.note: Push notifications say only that something changed, and each channel expires and must be replaced.

limits.text: Push notification channels expire (after a week by default) and nothing renews them; a new watch call must replace each one.
Requests are limited to 600 a minute per user and 10,000 a minute per project.
Outflare reads one calendar every 15 minutes with sync tokens and doesn't use push notifications yet.

name: Outlook Calendar
summary: Count meetings booked with leads, from a Microsoft 365 or Outlook.com calendar.
description: Reads the signed-in person's calendar and keeps only meetings with a lead or a lead's colleague among the attendees. Nothing is written to the calendar.
pricing: Free

features.note: Change notification subscriptions expire after a few days and must be renewed.

limits.text: Change notification subscriptions for calendar events expire after a few days and must be renewed.
Outlook allows 10,000 requests per app and mailbox in 10 minutes, and 4 at the same time.
Where an organisation has turned off user consent, an admin must approve the app before anyone can connect.
Outflare reads calendar changes every 15 minutes with delta queries and doesn't subscribe to change notifications yet.

name: GitHub
summary: Know when your website's repository ships, so fixes are re-checked and experiments start on the real deploy.
description: Reads your repositories' production deployments, or pushes to the default branch when a repository records no deployments. Outflare never pushes code, opens pull requests or changes settings through it.
pricing: Works on every GitHub plan, including free

features.note: The API records a deployment; your own CI or host does the actual deploy.
Fine-grained tokens can read Deployments only; OAuth sign-in has no read-only scope for private repositories.

limits.text: OAuth apps have no read-only scope for private repositories, so signing in asks for full repo access.
A user's token gets 5,000 REST API requests an hour; calls over that fail until the hour resets.
GitHub can send deployment_status webhooks; Outflare checks for new deploys every five minutes instead.

name: Vercel
summary: Know when your website's Vercel project goes live, so fixes are re-checked and experiments start on the real deploy.
description: Reads your projects' production deployments and the domains they serve. Outflare never deploys, promotes, rolls back or changes settings through it.
pricing: Works on every Vercel plan, including Hobby

features.note: Account webhooks need a Pro or Enterprise plan.
Sign in with Vercel permissions for API requests are in private beta; Outflare uses an access token.
Tokens can be limited to an account, team or project, not to reading.

limits.text: Access tokens can be limited to an account, team or project, but not to read-only access.
Account webhooks, including deployment events, need a Pro or Enterprise plan.
Sign in with Vercel API permissions are in private beta, so connecting needs a token made in the Vercel dashboard.
Vercel can send deployment webhooks; Outflare checks for new deploys every five minutes instead.

name: Attio
summary: Bring your Attio CRM over: see every object, field and list it holds, then import it once.
description: Reads your Attio workspace's objects (People, Companies, Deals and custom ones), their fields, lists and pipelines, and counts records, entries, notes and tasks, so you can see what moving over brings before anything is copied. Read-only: Outflare never changes anything in Attio.
pricing: Works on every Attio plan, including Free

features.note: Custom objects need the Pro or Enterprise plan.

limits.text: The API allows 100 read and 25 write requests a second, and listing records also counts against a score shared by all apps.
Custom objects need the Pro or Enterprise plan; the Free plan allows 3 objects and 50,000 records.
Enriched values can't be overwritten over the API, and some are hidden from it depending on the plan.
The SQL query endpoint needs an Enterprise plan and is limited to 2 requests a second.
Outflare imports Attio once and doesn't follow later changes or use Attio's webhooks yet.
Outflare counts list entries, notes and tasks but doesn't import them yet.

name: HubSpot
summary: Count meetings and deals from outreach, and log booked meetings on the contact.
description: Reads deals (stage, amount, close date) and meetings, and ties each to the lead and campaign that started it. Optionally writes meetings booked from outreach onto the HubSpot contact (off by default, since HubSpot may already log them from its own calendar sync), and replies with the labels you pick as a note on the contact, with a task to follow up. Journeys can create or update contacts (a push to CRM step). Deals are never changed.
pricing: Works on every HubSpot plan, including free

features.note: Public apps manage subscriptions over the API; a private app's are set in its settings in HubSpot.
Custom objects need an Enterprise subscription.

limits.text: Private apps on Free and Starter get 100 requests per 10 seconds and 250,000 a day per account.
CRM search is limited to 5 requests a second and 10,000 results per query, and sends no rate limit headers.
Custom objects and their pipelines need an Enterprise subscription.
A private app's webhook subscriptions are set in its settings in HubSpot; the API can't change them.
Outflare reads deals and meetings every 15 minutes and doesn't use HubSpot webhooks yet.

name: Apollo
summary: Search Apollo's people database and reveal work emails with your Apollo credits.
description: Build lists from Apollo searches by title, seniority, company size, industry and location. Searching is free; revealing an email uses one Apollo credit per person found. Mailboxes also connected in Apollo are flagged on the Mailboxes page, since Apollo may send from them too.
pricing: Free search; one credit per revealed email

features.note: Mobile numbers are sent later to a webhook, not in the response, and cost extra credits.
Up to 10 people per request.

limits.text: People search returns no emails or phone numbers; each one needs a separate enrichment call that spends credits.
People search shows at most 50,000 records for one search (100 per page, 500 pages).
Mobile numbers are delivered minutes later to a public HTTPS webhook, not in the response, and cost 8 more credits each.
Free accounts must be registered with a work email address to use people search and enrichment over the API.
Outflare enriches one person per call and doesn't use bulk enrichment, which takes up to 10 people per request.
Outflare doesn't request mobile numbers from Apollo.

name: Findymail
summary: Find verified work emails from a name and company domain.
description: Fills in verified work emails for people found elsewhere. Charges only when it finds one.
pricing: One credit per email found

features.note: Finds people by role at one company domain; there is no search across companies.
From a LinkedIn URL, and only for contacts outside the EU.
One person per request, but requests can run asynchronously with a webhook, up to 300 at once.

limits.text: Phone numbers are found only for contacts outside the EU, and cost 10 credits each.
Asynchronous jobs can take up to 24 hours to process, depending on Findymail's workload.
Finding emails by company domain allows only 5 concurrent requests when used synchronously.
Outflare finds emails from a name and company domain only; it doesn't use Findymail's LinkedIn, phone or role searches.

name: LeadMagic
summary: Find work emails from a name and company domain.
description: Fills in work emails for people found elsewhere. Charges only when it finds a valid address.
pricing: One credit per email found

features.note: Bulk jobs report back to a webhook when done.

limits.text: On the Essential and Growth plans, people search over the API costs 1 credit per person returned.
Outflare uses LeadMagic only to find emails; it doesn't use its people search to build lists.
Outflare doesn't look up mobile numbers, which cost 5 credits each.

name: MoltSets
summary: Search B2B people and find valid work emails with your own MoltSets plan.
description: Build lists from MoltSets people searches by title, seniority, industry, company size, country, company domain and keywords, and find work emails from a LinkedIn URL, an email, or a name with a company domain. Each email carries MoltSets' send-safety grade.
pricing: Flat monthly plans with fair-use limits; a free tier of 1,000 tokens

features.note: Needs the Phone Tokens add-on on a paid plan.
Enrichment tools take up to 100 values per call.

limits.text: Every plan has fair-use caps on records and requests per 5-hour window and on records per week.
Mobile numbers need Phone Tokens, a separate monthly add-on to a paid plan.
Outflare looks up one person per call and doesn't use batch requests or mobile number lookups.
MoltSets can name the company behind an IP address; Outflare doesn't use it for website visitors.

name: People Data Labs
summary: Search and enrich people from People Data Labs with your own credits.
description: Build lists from People Data Labs searches by title, seniority, industry, company size and location, and fill in missing fields on leads you already have.
pricing: One credit per person returned; one per company found from a website visitor's address

features.note: Bulk enrichment takes up to 100 people per request.

limits.text: On the free plan, emails, phone numbers and addresses are hidden; the Pro plan unlocks them.
Person Search allows 10 requests per minute by default.
Each person a search returns uses one credit, whether or not it has an email.
Free accounts can make 100 Person Enrichment requests per minute; paid accounts get 1,000.
Outflare enriches one person per call and doesn't use the bulk enrichment endpoint.

name: Prospeo
summary: Find verified work emails from a name and company, or a LinkedIn URL.
description: Fills in work emails for people found elsewhere. Only verified addresses are returned, and you are charged only when one is found.
pricing: One credit per email found

features.note: Up to 50 people per request.

limits.text: The search API allows 1 request per second, 30 per minute and 1,000 per day on the Starter plan.
The free plan has limited API access and 100 credits a month.
Some search filters, such as job changes, need the Growth plan.
Search costs 1 credit per page of up to 25 results and returns no contact data; verified mobile numbers cost 10 credits.
Outflare uses Prospeo only to find emails; it doesn't use its people search to build lists.
Outflare enriches one person per call and doesn't request mobile numbers or use bulk enrichment.

name: Snitcher
summary: Find the companies behind your website's visitors with your own Snitcher IP to Company key.
description: Outflare sends Snitcher the address of each new visitor who accepted your site's cookies, once a day at most, and adds the company to your CRM. Addresses of homes, phones, data centres and VPNs name nobody. Checking the key looks up one public address.
pricing: Per lookup, on your Snitcher plan

features.note: One IP address per request.

limits.text: The IP to Company API is sold apart from Snitcher's standard plans; an API key comes through Snitcher's sales team.
The API names companies only; it returns no people, emails or phone numbers.

name: Cloudflare
summary: Add the DNS records Outflare needs (site verification, sending and tracking domains) in one click.
description: Outflare only adds records, each with the comment "Added by Outflare": it never changes or deletes one. With an API token, use the "Edit zone DNS" template, limited to the zones you want Outflare to write to.
pricing: Free

name: Amazon SES
summary: Send transactional and lifecycle email from your own AWS account, at about $0.10 per 1,000 emails.
description: Outflare sends through your Amazon SES account with an IAM access key. It registers your domain with Easy DKIM and a custom MAIL FROM subdomain, and sets up a configuration set and an SNS topic so deliveries, bounces and complaints come back automatically. SES is for mail people asked for: never cold email.
pricing: Pay AWS directly: about $0.10 per 1,000 emails

name: Postmark
summary: Send transactional email through Postmark, known for fast, reliable delivery of receipts and password resets.
description: Outflare sends through one of your Postmark servers and registers a webhook on it, so deliveries, bounces and spam complaints come back automatically. Add the account token too and Outflare also adds your sending domain with its DKIM and return-path records.
pricing: Pay Postmark directly; 100 test emails a month free

name: Resend
summary: Send transactional and lifecycle email through Resend, the developer-first email API.
description: Outflare sends through your Resend account, adds your sending domain with its DKIM, SPF and MX records, and registers a signed webhook so deliveries, bounces and complaints come back automatically.
pricing: Pay Resend directly; 3,000 emails a month free

name: Bouncer
summary: EU-hosted email verification with toxicity checks.
description: Verifies each address and reports catch-all, disposable and role accounts, with a 0–100 score.
pricing: Pay per credit

limits.text: Creating batches is limited to 60 a minute, with up to 25 batches processed at once.
Reading the credit balance is limited to 10 requests a minute.
Outflare checks addresses one at a time and doesn't use Bouncer's batch API yet.

name: DeBounce
summary: Email verification that marks addresses safe to send, risky or invalid.
description: Verifies each address and flags spam traps, disposable, catch-all and role addresses.
pricing: Pay per credit

features.note: Webhooks are advertised, but the bulk API reference describes checking a list's status by polling.

limits.text: A regular API key allows 5 calls at once, or 2 with data enrichment on; more return HTTP 429.
Only one bulk validation job runs per account at a time; further uploads wait in a queue.
Outflare checks addresses one at a time and doesn't use DeBounce's bulk API yet.

name: Emailable
summary: Email verification with a quality score for every address.
description: Verifies each address and returns a state, a reason and a 0–100 score.
pricing: Pay per credit

limits.text: Each endpoint has its own rate limit, and higher limits need an enterprise account.
Outflare checks addresses one at a time and doesn't use Emailable's batch API yet.

name: Hunter
summary: Find and verify work emails with Hunter.
description: Verifies each address with SMTP checks and a confidence score.
pricing: Monthly plans with search and verification credits

features.note: The Email Verifier API takes one address per call.

limits.text: The Email Verifier API takes one address per call and has no batch endpoint.
Email verification is limited to 10 requests a second and 300 a minute per API key or IP.
Greylisted addresses return HTTP 202 and must be checked again later, sometimes hours later.

name: MillionVerifier
summary: Low-cost email verification popular with cold email teams.
description: Verifies each address and marks catch-all, disposable and role addresses.
pricing: Pay per credit

features.note: No callback is documented; a file's status is checked by polling.

limits.text: Outflare checks addresses one at a time with the single API and doesn't use the bulk file API yet.

name: NeverBounce
summary: Real-time email verification with a deliverability guarantee.
description: Verifies each address and flags disposable and catch-all domains.
pricing: Pay per credit

limits.text: A bulk job held for manual review can take up to one business day to be released.
Requests larger than 25 MB are refused with HTTP 413.
Outflare checks addresses one at a time and doesn't use NeverBounce's bulk jobs yet.

name: Reoon Email Verifier
summary: Low-cost verification with a power mode that checks the mailbox over SMTP.
description: Verifies each address in power mode and flags catch-all, disposable, role and full mailboxes.
pricing: Pay per credit; unknown results are refunded

features.note: In power mode, which Outflare uses; quick mode skips the deep check.
No callback is documented; a task's status is checked by polling.

limits.text: Single checks should not run in more than 5 parallel threads continuously.
Outflare checks addresses one at a time and doesn't use Reoon's bulk verification tasks yet.

name: ZeroBounce
summary: Email validation with spam-trap, abuse and catch-all detection.
description: Checks each address before it is emailed and flags spam traps, known complainers and catch-all domains.
pricing: Pay per credit

limits.text: The batch endpoint takes up to 200 addresses a call and 5 calls a minute; going over blocks it for 10 minutes.
The credit balance endpoint allows 80,000 requests an hour; going over blocks access for a day.
Outflare checks addresses one at a time and doesn't use ZeroBounce's batch or file upload APIs yet.

name: Cheap Inboxes
summary: Import your Google and Microsoft mailboxes from Cheap Inboxes and keep them in sync.
description: Connect your Cheap Inboxes account with an API key. Outflare lists every mailbox, imports the ones you pick (or all of them, automatically) with their passwords, checks SMTP, IMAP and DNS, and picks up new and cancelled mailboxes on its own. Google mailboxes get an app password from Cheap Inboxes, since Google refuses plain passwords.
pricing: You pay Cheap Inboxes directly

name: Gmail
summary: Add Gmail and Google Workspace mailboxes without passwords.
description: Sign in to one mailbox, or connect a service account with domain-wide delegation for https://mail.google.com/ to add any mailbox of your Google Workspace by its address. Mailboxes send and read mail over SMTP and IMAP with OAuth.
pricing: Free

name: Outlook
summary: Add Outlook and Microsoft 365 mailboxes without passwords.
description: Sign in to one mailbox, or connect an Entra app with the Exchange Online application permissions IMAP.AccessAsApp and SMTP.SendAsApp to add any mailbox of your tenant by its address. Mailboxes send and read mail over SMTP and IMAP with OAuth.
pricing: Free

name: Claude
summary: Plan and run missions from a goal you type, with your own Claude API key. Anthropic's Claude models.
description: Outflare sends the model the goal, the company context and a summary of the workspace (mailbox capacity, lead counts, campaigns, connectors) to plan, and the mission's progress and API answers while Outflare's agent runs it. Your key is encrypted, only ever sent to Claude's own API, and never shown again, logged or given to the model. Usage is billed to your Claude account; set a monthly limit under Settings → AI model.
pricing: Pay per token, billed by Claude

limits.text: Each usage tier has a monthly spend cap ($500 on the Start tier); at the cap, API calls fail until the next month.
New organisations may start on an Evaluation tier with lower limits, which rise as usage history builds.
Your own monthly spend limit, below the tier's cap, is set on the Billing page of the Claude Console.
The Message Batches API halves the price of calls that can wait; Outflare sends every call on its own.

name: DeepSeek
summary: Plan and run missions from a goal you type, with your own DeepSeek API key. DeepSeek's low-cost models, hosted in China.
description: Outflare sends the model the goal, the company context and a summary of the workspace (mailbox capacity, lead counts, campaigns, connectors) to plan, and the mission's progress and API answers while Outflare's agent runs it. Your key is encrypted, only ever sent to DeepSeek's own API, and never shown again, logged or given to the model. Usage is billed to your DeepSeek account; set a monthly limit under Settings → AI model.
pricing: Pay per token, billed by DeepSeek

features.note: In the Responses API and a separate Search API; Chat Completions takes function tools only.
No batch endpoint in the docs; off-peak hours cost half.

limits.text: Each account has a cap on requests in flight per model (500 for deepseek-v4-pro); calls over it get HTTP 429.
Calls on weekdays from 01:00 to 04:00 and 06:00 to 10:00 UTC are billed at peak rates, twice the off-peak price.
Web search runs in DeepSeek's Responses API or its Search API; Outflare calls Chat Completions, so its DeepSeek calls don't search.

name: Gemini
summary: Plan and run missions from a goal you type, with your own Gemini API key. Google's Gemini models.
description: Outflare sends the model the goal, the company context and a summary of the workspace (mailbox capacity, lead counts, campaigns, connectors) to plan, and the mission's progress and API answers while Outflare's agent runs it. Your key is encrypted, only ever sent to Gemini's own API, and never shown again, logged or given to the model. Usage is billed to your Gemini account; set a monthly limit under Settings → AI model.
pricing: Pay per token, billed by Gemini

limits.text: On the free tier, Google uses prompts and answers to improve its products; linking a billing account stops that.
Apps used by people in the EEA, Switzerland or the UK must use only the paid service, with billing linked.
Tier 1 needs a linked billing account and is capped at $250; at the cap, calls pause until the next billing cycle.
Grounding with Google Search lets Gemini search the web; Outflare doesn't turn it on for Gemini yet.

name: Mistral
summary: Plan and run missions from a goal you type, with your own Mistral API key. Mistral's models, hosted in the EU.
description: Outflare sends the model the goal, the company context and a summary of the workspace (mailbox capacity, lead counts, campaigns, connectors) to plan, and the mission's progress and API answers while Outflare's agent runs it. Your key is encrypted, only ever sent to Mistral's own API, and never shown again, logged or given to the model. Usage is billed to your Mistral account; set a monthly limit under Settings → AI model.
pricing: Pay per token, billed by Mistral

features.note: Conversations and Agents APIs only, not Chat Completions.

limits.text: Free mode has the lowest rate limits; higher limits need pay-as-you-go billing and grow with total spend.
Web search needs Mistral's Conversations or Agents API; Outflare calls Chat Completions, so its Mistral calls don't search.

name: OpenAI
summary: Plan and run missions from a goal you type, with your own OpenAI API key. OpenAI's GPT models.
description: Outflare sends the model the goal, the company context and a summary of the workspace (mailbox capacity, lead counts, campaigns, connectors) to plan, and the mission's progress and API answers while Outflare's agent runs it. Your key is encrypted, only ever sent to OpenAI's own API, and never shown again, logged or given to the model. Usage is billed to your OpenAI account; set a monthly limit under Settings → AI model.
pricing: Pay per token, billed by OpenAI

limits.text: Monthly usage is capped by tier, starting at $500 a month after the first $5 of credit, and rises as total purchases grow.
Some models and features need organisation verification, done in the OpenAI dashboard with a government ID.
Any model can search with the Responses API's web search tool; Outflare uses Chat Completions, where only search models search.
The Batch API halves the price of calls that can wait a day; Outflare sends every call on its own.

name: OpenRouter
summary: Plan and run missions from a goal you type, with your own OpenRouter API key. Hundreds of models from many vendors (OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI, Perplexity...) with one key; OpenRouter reports what each call cost.
description: Outflare sends the model the goal, the company context and a summary of the workspace (mailbox capacity, lead counts, campaigns, connectors) to plan, and the mission's progress and API answers while Outflare's agent runs it. Your key is encrypted, only ever sent to OpenRouter's own API, and never shown again, logged or given to the model. Usage is billed to your OpenRouter account; set a monthly limit under Settings → AI model.
pricing: Pay per token, billed by OpenRouter

limits.text: Free model variants allow 50 requests a day, or 1,000 a day once the account has bought $10 of credits.
Credits are prepaid, with a 5.5% fee added when you buy them on the standard plan.
The Batch API runs calls that can wait at about half the price; Outflare sends every call on its own.

name: Requesty
summary: Plan and run missions from a goal you type, with your own Requesty API key. Models from many vendors with one Requesty key, with its own spending limits and fallbacks.
description: Outflare sends the model the goal, the company context and a summary of the workspace (mailbox capacity, lead counts, campaigns, connectors) to plan, and the mission's progress and API answers while Outflare's agent runs it. Your key is encrypted, only ever sent to Requesty's own API, and never shown again, logged or given to the model. Usage is billed to your Requesty account; set a monthly limit under Settings → AI model.
pricing: Pay per token, billed by Requesty

features.note: Not described in Requesty's docs.
No batch endpoint in the docs.

limits.text: Requests in flight are capped at your balance in dollars times a tier multiplier; calls over it get HTTP 429.
Free models allow a new organisation 200 requests a day and 20 a minute.

name: Vercel AI Gateway
summary: Plan and run missions from a goal you type, with your own Vercel AI Gateway API key. Models from many vendors with one Vercel key, billed to your Vercel team.
description: Outflare sends the model the goal, the company context and a summary of the workspace (mailbox capacity, lead counts, campaigns, connectors) to plan, and the mission's progress and API answers while Outflare's agent runs it. Your key is encrypted, only ever sent to Vercel AI Gateway's own API, and never shown again, logged or given to the model. Usage is billed to your Vercel AI Gateway account; set a monthly limit under Settings → AI model.
pricing: Pay per token, billed by Vercel AI Gateway

features.note: Not confirmed; no batch endpoint found in the AI Gateway docs.

limits.text: The free tier's $5 monthly credit covers only some models, at lower rate limits; buying credits ends it.
Search tools such as Perplexity Search are added to a call as server tools; Outflare doesn't use them yet.

name: xAI
summary: Plan and run missions from a goal you type, with your own xAI API key. xAI's Grok models.
description: Outflare sends the model the goal, the company context and a summary of the workspace (mailbox capacity, lead counts, campaigns, connectors) to plan, and the mission's progress and API answers while Outflare's agent runs it. Your key is encrypted, only ever sent to xAI's own API, and never shown again, logged or given to the model. Usage is billed to your xAI account; set a monthly limit under Settings → AI model.
pricing: Pay per token, billed by xAI

limits.text: Outflare calls Chat Completions, which xAI has deprecated and which runs function tools only; web search needs the Responses API.

name: Slack
summary: Post alerts, such as hot replies and hot website visitors, to a Slack channel.
description: Posts each alert you choose to a channel in your own Slack workspace, with a link to it in Outflare. Outflare only posts; it never reads your messages.
pricing: Works on every Slack plan, including free

name: Tolt
summary: Move your referral or affiliate program over from Tolt.
description: Reads your Tolt program: partners of every status with their link codes, promo codes, referred customers, transactions and commissions, paid or not. Run the import as often as you like until the day you switch: each run brings only what changed. Outflare never changes anything in Tolt.
pricing: Free: Tolt does not charge for API calls

features.note: Some accounts' API doesn't list groups or flows.

name: Stripe
summary: See who pays you: customers, subscriptions, payments and refunds on each person's record.
description: Reads your Stripe customers, subscriptions, payments and refunds, every few minutes. Each customer becomes a person with their plan, monthly revenue, lifetime revenue and billing status, and each payment is an event on their timeline, so the CRM, lifecycle email, missions and partners all use the same numbers. Outflare never charges, refunds or changes payments in Stripe; the one thing it can create is a promotion code for a partner, for a coupon you already have, when your key allows it.
pricing: Free: Stripe does not charge for API calls

name: Ahrefs
summary: Domain Rating, backlinks, organic keywords, competitors and Site Audit health for your domains.
description: Needs an Ahrefs plan with API access and an API key. Reads Site Explorer for any domain and Site Audit for projects your account already crawls. Calls spend Ahrefs API units; Outflare records an estimate of each call in Outcomes and stops at the connection's monthly budget.
pricing: API units from your Ahrefs plan

features.note: SERP Overview returns the top 100 results from Ahrefs' own data.
Reads projects already set up in the Ahrefs app.

limits.text: API access needs a Lite plan or higher, and each plan has a fixed number of API units a month.
Each request costs at least 50 API units, and the cost grows with the rows and fields returned.
Site Audit projects are set up only in the Ahrefs app; the API reads existing projects.
The API allows 60 requests a minute by default and may refuse more when Ahrefs is under high load.
Lite, Standard and Advanced plans have fixed API units per billing cycle; buying more is for Enterprise.
Ahrefs can create Rank Tracker projects and return SERP overviews; Outflare doesn't use them yet.

name: Chrome UX Report
summary: Real-user Core Web Vitals and weekly field history.
description: Enable the Chrome UX Report and History APIs in your Google Cloud project and connect your own API key. Low-traffic pages may have no field data.
pricing: Your Google Cloud API quota

limits.text: Pages and origins without enough Chrome traffic return no data.
The API allows 150 queries a minute per Google Cloud project, shared with the History API, and the quota can't be raised.
Current data is a rolling 28-day average, so a change takes weeks to show in full.
History updates weekly, on Mondays, and goes back at most 40 weeks.
Each call reads one origin or URL.

name: DataForSEO
summary: Keyword rankings, rank tracking, estimated search traffic, competitors and backlinks for any domain, paid per call.
description: Uses DataForSEO Labs for rankings, traffic and competitors, the SERP API to track where your pages rank on Google, and the Backlinks API for links (a separate DataForSEO subscription; without it the overview skips links). Every call's cost comes back from DataForSEO and is recorded in Outcomes; a monthly budget on the connection stops calls before they go over.
pricing: Pay per call, about $0.01 to $0.05 a report

features.note: The OnPage Lighthouse API runs lab tests, not real-user measurements.
The OnPage API crawls and parses pages for audits.
Task-based calls take a pingback or postback URL; live calls answer directly.

limits.text: Calls are paid from a prepaid balance, topped up from $50.
The API takes up to 2,000 calls a minute and 30 at the same time, unless DataForSEO raises it.
DataForSEO's OnPage API can crawl and audit a site; Outflare doesn't use it yet.

name: Geonode
summary: Searches the web, tracks where your pages rank on Google, finds your brands' social links, reads public X follower counts, and reads your own site's pages when a firewall blocks OutflareBot.
description: Runs web searches for finding companies and pages, through Geonode's Search API. Checks where your pages rank on Google for the keywords you track, through Geonode's Google Search Light API (one credit per results page; a check reads 10 pages), within the monthly budget you set on the connection. Reads each brand's homepage to suggest its social profiles and app store listings, and the public X profile in each brand's links once a day for its follower count. For sites you have proved you own, and only for pages robots.txt allows: when a page answers with a firewall block or a challenge, OutflareBot reads it through Geonode's Scraper API instead. Searches and pages cost Geonode tokens on your account.
pricing: Tokens per search and per page, and a credit per Google results page, on your Geonode plan

limits.text: The free plan allows one request at a time and 1,500 requests a month; more needs a paid plan.
Requests over the plan's concurrency limit fail with a 429 error.
Geonode's Crawl API can read a whole site in one job; Outflare reads single pages.

name: EmailBison
summary: Let Outflare decide which sender emails each EmailBison campaign uses.
description: Outflare reads your sender emails and campaigns every few minutes, adds and removes sender emails on campaigns as mailbox allocation decides, and accepts changes you make in EmailBison as manual ones. Replies your campaigns get come into the Outflare inbox, labelled, and you can answer them there.

features.note: Campaigns can be created; no endpoint was found to add sequence steps.
No endpoint to buy mailboxes was found in the API docs.

limits.text: Outflare doesn't import EmailBison campaigns and leads yet, though the API lists both.

name: Instantly
summary: Switching from Instantly? Import campaigns, leads and sending accounts in one go.
description: Reads your Instantly campaigns (with every step and variant), their leads and where each lead got to, and your sending accounts. Importing only reads. Once connected, mailbox allocation also adds and removes sending accounts on Instantly campaigns, and accepts changes you make in Instantly as manual ones.
pricing: Included in Instantly's Hypergrowth plan and above

features.note: Hypergrowth plan or above.
API v2 lists done-for-you email account orders; not checked in detail.

limits.text: Webhooks need the Hypergrowth plan or above.
Listing Unibox emails allows 20 requests a minute, fewer than most other endpoints.
Turning on warm-up starts a background job that must be polled, and takes at most 100 addresses in a list per call.
Outflare doesn't read or answer Instantly replies yet, though the API can.
Outflare imports Instantly campaigns but doesn't create them there, though the API can.

name: Smartlead
summary: Switching from Smartlead? Import campaigns, leads and email accounts in one go.
description: Reads your Smartlead campaigns (with every step and variant), their leads and where each lead got to, and your email accounts. Importing only reads. Once connected, mailbox allocation also adds and removes email accounts on Smartlead campaigns, and accepts changes you make in Smartlead as manual ones.

limits.text: API access and webhooks need the Pro plan or above; the Base plan has neither.
On the standard tier, a key may make 60 requests a minute and 1,000 an hour across all endpoints.
Lead statistics and lead activity endpoints allow 10 requests every 60 seconds.
Mailboxes can't be added to a domain bought through SmartSenders; only new domains with mailboxes can be ordered.
Outflare doesn't read or answer Smartlead replies yet, though the API can.

name: RB2B
summary: People visiting your website, by name, from your own RB2B account.
description: Connect it, then paste the webhook address from Visitors → Settings into RB2B's webhook integration. Each person RB2B names becomes a person in your CRM marked for review and tagged as from RB2B. Nobody is emailed until you approve them.
pricing: On your RB2B plan

name: Vector
summary: Contacts who visit your website, from your own Vector account.
description: Connect it, then add the webhook address from Visitors → Settings in Vector for the contact.visited event. Each person Vector names becomes a person in your CRM marked for review and tagged as from Vector. Nobody is emailed until you approve them.
pricing: On your Vector plan

limits.text: Webhook endpoints and the events they send are set up in Vector's app, with up to 10 segments per endpoint.
Outflare takes only contact.visited events and doesn't use Vector's other webhook events yet.

name: Warmly
summary: Identified contacts on your website, from your own Warmly account.
description: Connect it, then add the webhook address from Visitors → Settings in Warmly's webhook settings. Each person Warmly names becomes a person in your CRM marked for review and tagged as from Warmly. Nobody is emailed until you approve them.
pricing: On your Warmly plan

features.note: The free plan sends every visitor, unfiltered, to one webhook; filters need a paid plan.

limits.text: The free plan sends every person-level visitor, unfiltered, to one webhook; filtering and more destinations need a paid plan.
Outflare takes the people Warmly names and doesn't use its company-level visit events yet.

name: Engain
summary: Run Reddit campaigns through Engain's accounts: comments, replies, posts, threads and upvotes.
description: Uses your own Engain API key, so tasks and votes are billed to your Engain credits. Connecting checks the key and shows your projects and credits left. API access needs Engain's Max plan.
pricing: Engain credits: about 5 per comment or reply, 10 per post, 0.1 per upvote

features.note: Posts go out from Engain's own Reddit accounts, not the brand's.
Status and votes for the comments and posts Engain placed.
Suggests Reddit threads to join, not a full keyword search.
Replies go out from Engain's own Reddit accounts.
Needs the Max plan; tasks and votes spend Engain credits.

limits.text: API access needs Engain's Max plan.
An upvote order takes 1 to 20 votes a day and at most 2,000 in total, or 100 at high speed.
When a post is removed, only the upvotes not yet delivered come back as credits.
Engain's API returns recommended upvote goals for a Reddit link; Outflare doesn't use them yet.

name: LinkedIn
summary: Track followers and posts of your company pages and profile, and post from them.
description: Sign in with your own LinkedIn account: Outflare reaches your profile and every company page you administer. LinkedIn's API is free; on a self-hosted server, register a LinkedIn app with the Community Management API and set CONNECTOR_LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID and CONNECTOR_LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET.
pricing: Free

features.note: Company page posts; a person's own posts can't be listed without a restricted permission.
Comments through the Community Management API.
Free, but the Community Management API needs LinkedIn's review first.

limits.text: The Community Management API needs an application LinkedIn reviews, and it must be the only product on its app.
Until an app passes review for the Standard tier, it gets 500 calls a day and 100 per member.
Listing a person's own posts needs r_member_social, a restricted permission given only to approved apps.
Like, comment and share webhook events fire only for public posts.
LinkedIn's API can comment on posts and send comment webhooks; Outflare doesn't use them yet.

name: Reddit
summary: Find threads where your brand can help, and post approved replies from your brand's own account.
description: Uses your own Reddit app, so searches and posts run on your Reddit API access. Make a web app at reddit.com/prefs/apps with this server's redirect URI, paste its client id and secret, then sign in with the brand's Reddit account to post replies a person approved. Every reply says who wrote it.
pricing: Reddit's Data API terms apply to your app

features.note: Scores and comment counts.
Karma and subreddit subscriber counts.
Free up to 100 queries a minute; commercial use needs Reddit's written approval.

limits.text: Developers must request access and get Reddit's approval before using the API.
Commercial use of the API needs Reddit's written approval and a contract.
Free use allows 100 queries a minute per OAuth client id, averaged over 10 minutes.
Accounts that post automatically must register as apps and carry Reddit's App label.

name: X
summary: Track your brand's X followers and posts, and post from its own account.
description: Uses your own X developer app, so X bills your account for API use (pay per use). Make an app in the X developer console with OAuth 2.0 turned on (type: web app) and this server's redirect URI, paste its OAuth 2.0 client id and secret, then sign in with the brand's X account.
pricing: X bills your developer account per use

features.note: Private metrics such as impressions only for your own posts from the last 30 days.
Recent search covers the last 7 days; full-archive search is a separate endpoint.
Pay per use, billed to the developer app's owner.

limits.text: API use is billed per request, such as $0.005 per post read, $0.015 per new post and $0.20 per post with a link.
Impressions, clicks and other private metrics are only available for posts from the last 30 days.
Account Activity webhooks on pay per use allow 3 subscriptions and 1 webhook.
X's API can search recent posts and post replies; Outflare doesn't use them yet.

name: Google Tag Manager
summary: Add Outflare's website script to your site in one click, through your own Tag Manager container.
description: Outflare adds one Custom HTML tag named "Outflare" that fires on all pages, in a Tag Manager workspace of its own, so nobody else's unpublished changes go live with it. It never edits or removes your other tags.
pricing: Free

name: Hotjar
summary: Hotjar's API covers surveys and user lookups, not traffic, so there is nothing to report yet.

name: Segment
summary: Segment forwards events but does not count visits. Planned as a source of events, not a report.

features.note: Segment forwards every event to warehouses and other tools; it keeps no traffic reports of its own.

name: Chili Piper
summary: Meetings booked through Chili Piper routers.

features.note: The API uses tokens an admin makes; OAuth is offered for its MCP server, to admins.

limits.text: API tokens are made by an admin in Chili Piper's Command Center, with permissions chosen per section.

name: SavvyCal
summary: Meetings booked through SavvyCal links.

limits.text: Personal access tokens are made in SavvyCal's developer settings, in the app.

name: Zoom Scheduler
summary: Meetings booked through Zoom Scheduler.

limits.text: Zoom Scheduler is a paid add-on for each user, unless the account's Zoom Workplace plan includes it.
The free Scheduler Basic leaves Zoom Workplace Basic and Pro from 3 November 2026, except for users who turned it on before 4 September 2026.
An admin assigns a Scheduler licence to each user in Zoom's admin settings.

name: Pipedrive
summary: Create deals in Pipedrive from interested replies.

features.note: Custom fields on deals, people, organisations and products only.

limits.text: Each company has a daily token budget (30,000 times a plan multiplier times seats), and each call spends tokens; a search costs 40.
Bursts are limited per token, from 20 requests per 2 seconds on Lite to 120 on Ultimate, and search to 10 per 2 seconds.
A user can have at most 40 webhooks.

name: Salesforce
summary: Sync replies, interested leads and meetings to Salesforce.

features.note: Group, Essentials and Professional editions don't include API access.
Change Data Capture streams changes; without an add-on it covers 5 objects.

limits.text: Group, Essentials and Professional editions don't include API access; Professional needs the Web Services API add-on.
Enterprise edition allows 100,000 API calls plus 1,000 per full licence in a rolling 24 hours.
Without an add-on, Change Data Capture covers 5 objects and delivers 25,000 events a day in Enterprise edition.

name: BetterContact
summary: Waterfall email and phone finding.

features.note: Up to 100 leads per request.

limits.text: Enrichment is asynchronous; results come to a webhook or by polling, never in the first response.
Each API key allows 100 requests per minute on Starter, free and small plans, and 200 on Pro.
Submitting enrichment isn't idempotent; retrying a request that already succeeded enriches and charges again.

name: Clay

name: Cognism
summary: Search Cognism's European-strong contact data.

features.note: Which fields come back beyond core contact data depends on the package.
Search returns up to 100 records per call; redeem takes up to 20.

limits.text: The API needs a Cognism package that includes API access; it sets the fields, search tokens and rate limits.
API credentials are created by signing in to Cognism, under Settings, M2M Connect.
Each contact redeemed costs 1 credit, and each enriched profile uses 1 from the preview allowance.
Redeem takes 1 to 20 records per call, so revealing a large list needs many calls.
